# F-35I "Adir" damage model

*Generated by `scripts/damage/make_report.py` from `scripts/damage/f35_damage.py` and the hitboxes measured on the Blender model (`data/damage_model.json`). Do not edit by hand.*

The model is destructible at three levels:

1. **Hitboxes.** 30 damage components, each with hit points and an oriented box fitted to the Blender geometry (`HB_<component>` wire boxes in the *Hitboxes* collection, hidden in renders).
2. **Damage state.** Health 0..1 per component, stored as `health_<component>` on the `F35I_Rig` object, so it can be keyframed. Hits (point, ray, blast) are turned into health loss through the hitboxes.
3. **Effects.** `evaluate(state, Mach, altitude)` computes the flight attributes for a damage state. In Blender the same health values drive what you see: soot, impact scorches, smoke, fuel vapour, parts breaking off and tumbling away, a gear leg folding.

All reference values come from public sources (see `docs/research.md`). Where the real figure is not public, the value is a typical fighter value and is marked **model**. The transonic drag rise is calibrated so the intact jet just reaches Mach 1.6 at 11 km (calibrated peak CD0 = 0.0713).

| Endurance at that condition (90 % of fuel) | 93.5 min | model |
| Bank needed to fly straight | 0.0° | computed |

Model assumptions (not public): lift-curve slope 3.6/rad, CLmax 1.55, subsonic CD0 0.028, induced-drag factor 0.15, roll damping Clp -0.32, dihedral effect Clβ -0.1/rad, side force CYβ -0.95/rad, max trim sideslip 8.0°, the flight control system keeps 40 % of roll authority in reserve before it accepts sideslip.

**Hits.** A point hit gives 70 % of its damage to the smallest box that contains the point and shares the rest between the other boxes there. A blast loses damage linearly with the distance to each box. A part that breaks off takes its children with it (outer wing, LEF and flaperon go with the inner wing).

**Wing split measured on the mesh:** the outer panel (outboard of the tear line) carries 24.4 % of one wing's lift at 4.68 m from the centreline; the inner panel acts at 2.84 m. Body lift is 24 % of the total.

## 3. How damage changes the attributes

- **Thrust** = intact thrust × engine^1.2 (0 below 15 % = flame-out) × (mean inlet airflow)^1.3 × (0.8 + 0.2 × nozzle) × 0.5 if the fuel feed is below 25 %. The afterburner needs nozzle > 50 % and engine > 40 %.
- **Max speed** = lowest of: thrust = drag (drag polar with transonic rise, more drag from holes and missing parts, more induced drag when lift is lost), the Mach placard of damaged surfaces, the structure, and the 700 KCAS dynamic-pressure limit (reduced when parts are missing).
- **Lift and tilt.** Missing or damaged lifting surfaces shift the lift centre sideways; lost structure and leaked fuel shift the centre of mass. The flight control system trims the rolling moment with up to 60 % of its roll authority, then with sideslip (dihedral effect). A sideslip makes a side force, and to fly straight the jet must bank against it: tan φ = |CYβ| β / CL. That bank is the **tilt**, always towards the damaged side. If even full control and 8° of sideslip cannot hold the moment, the aircraft rolls off at p = ΔCl / |Clp| × 2V / b.
- **Lower speed means more tilt**, because the lift asymmetry grows with CL while the control power does not.
- **g-limit** from structure health and pitch authority (stabilators); **AoA limit** from fin health (Cnβ).
- **Fuel**: a damaged tank leaks 55 × damage^1.5 × √(capacity / 1600) kg/min; a tank in a part that breaks off is lost at once. The engine burn is drawn evenly from all tanks, so leaks create a lateral imbalance.
- **Systems**: radar, EOTS, DAS, avionics, gun, weapons, gear, canopy, pilot, electrical power. A failed power and thermal management system leaves the actuators on battery (60 % roll authority).

With the outer panel gone the jet can be held down to about 180 kt; with the whole wing gone it can be held down to about 370 kt. The tilt peaks just above the minimum control speed and fades as speed rises, because less lift (and so less lift asymmetry) is needed. For comparison, the IAF F-15D that landed without most of its right wing in 1983 was flown fast for the same reason.

## 7. Landing-gear collapse on the ground

Measured on the mesh: the jet pivots about the line through the two tyres that still stand until the first part of the airframe touches the ground.

| Broken leg | Roll | Pitch | Rotation | First contact (x, s, z) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| main_gear_L | +13.6° | +4.9° | 14.5° | 0.92, 12.05, -0.84 |
| main_gear_R | -13.5° | +5.0° | 14.5° | -0.92, 12.05, -0.84 |
| nose_gear | +0.0° | -8.0° | 8.0° | 0.03, 1.71, -0.56 |

Roll is positive with the left wing down, pitch positive nose up.

## 8. Using it

**Command line (no Blender):**

```
python3 scripts/damage/f35_damage.py --list
python3 scripts/damage/f35_damage.py --scenario outer_left_wing_lost --mach 0.4 --alt 0
python3 scripts/damage/f35_damage.py --set engine=0.5 inlet_R=0.3 --mach 0.9 --alt 9000
python3 scripts/damage/f35_damage.py --blast 1.2 9.5 0.3 400 3.0      # x s z HP radius
python3 scripts/damage/f35_damage.py --all
```

**In Blender** (after building with `scripts/build_f35i.py`):

- Set or keyframe `F35I_Rig["health_<component>"]` (0..1). Soot, smoke, fuel vapour and the folded gear leg follow at once; a part whose health reaches 0 is replaced by its torn stub.
- To make a part break off and tumble away at frame F, also set `break_frame_<component>` = F (or call `f35.destruct.break_off(component, F)`). Set `debris_ground` = 1 when parked, so the pieces fall onto the apron instead of streaming aft.
- `f35.destruct.impact(origin, direction, hp, frame)` ray-casts a hit, adds a scorch mark with glowing edges and lowers the health of the components inside the hitboxes. `blast(centre, hp, radius, frame)` does the same for a proximity blast.
- `f35.destruct.flight_response(frame, mach, alt)` runs the simulator on the current health and keys the bank (tilt), the sideslip and the side-stick, or a continuous roll if the jet cannot be held.
- `f35.destruct.collapse_gear("main_gear_L", frame)` drops the jet onto its wing using the measured attitude.

**Other tools:** `data/damage_model.json` holds the specification, every component with its hitbox, the wing split, the gear-collapse attitudes and the intact attributes.

## 9. Limits

This is an engineering-style model for animation and games, not flight-test data. Aerodynamic and control coefficients are typical values, not F-35 data; the structure, armour-free hit points and leak rates are invented but consistent. The trends (tilt grows as speed drops, a damaged inlet or engine caps the speed, a lost fin lowers the AoA limit) follow standard flight mechanics.
